chemistry_notes.text: Type II photosensitization: 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole absorbs at 420 nm, undergoes ISC to T1, sensitizes 3O2 to 1O2, which selectively oxidizes Fmoc-L-methionine thioether to sulfoxide. Key design decisions: (1) PFA tubing used (inventory constraint; PFA is transparent to visible light, compatible with MeCN, rated to 60°C and 10 bar). (2) 1 mm ID coil gives short optical path length for uniform photon delivery, addressing batch Beer-Lambert limitation. (3) Gas-liquid segmented flow with air MFC addresses O2 mass-transfer limitation (batch: headspace diffusion only). (4) BPR at 3.0 bar mandatory for gas-liquid system to maintain stable slug flow and prevent uncontrolled degassing. (5) Residence time set to ~4 min (inlet/STP basis) — longer than batch 5 min but justified by O2 transfer sufficiency warning (Da=92, O2 transfer 0.19× demand); screening at 2–8 min range recommended. (6) Analogies 1–3 are all single-phase photoredox (Ir/Ru, no gas co-feed) — not directly applicable for gas-liquid parameters; hardware parameters (FEP/PFA tubing, ~1–5 mL reactor, blue LED, 25–50°C) confirm general photochemistry flow setup. Residence time from analogies (12–30 min) is longer than our 5 min batch, so batch time is the primary anchor. (7) Over-oxidation to sulfone is a risk at long residence times — 4 min is conservative. (8) Incompatible pair: Fmoc + base — no base present, not a concern here.

controls.description: Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define and rehearse the emergency feed-stop sequence.
Segregate and label all process and flush waste by hazard class.
Leak- and pressure-test the assembled system before reagent introduction.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Cool and depressurize through the controlled outlet before opening the system.
Use the declared interlocked light enclosure when one is available; otherwise verify equivalent laboratory-approved light shielding before irradiation.
Exclude ignition sources and minimize oxygen-containing organic holdup.
Route oxygen-containing off-gas and solvent vapor to the declared compatible vent when one is available.

operating_procedure.instruction: Prepare Stream A: on a 4 mL final-volume basis, charge Fmoc-L-methionine: 0.4 mmol (0.1 M final); 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole: 0.04 mmol (0.01 M final); add acetonitrile to 4 mL total. Convert mmol to weighed/dispensed amount using the verified reagent MW, assay, and density recorded at preparation. The 4 mL basis is only the minimum consumed at the final feed rate during 16 min of commissioning and initial collection. Before preparation, add measured feed-line displacement, pump/reservoir hold-up and any extra startup or collection allowance. For an added duration, add this stream's flow rate multiplied by the extra minutes. Scale every solute amount and final solvent volume by the same factor to retain concentrations and reagent ratios. Confirm sufficient reagent availability and container capacity; no dead-volume allowance or available stock has been assumed. Provide priming and shutdown solvent separately. This schedule assumes continuous feeding; a finite sample-loop injection requires a separately specified loading and collection schedule.

parameter_bindings.minimum_stock_basis: continuous feed during commissioning plus initial collection

operating_procedure.instruction: Prepare Stream B: connect air to the assigned MFC at 2.66818 mL/min at STP on the declared STP basis (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar; 22.414 L/mol); no liquid stock is prepared.
Assemble only the inventory-assigned process graph and verify every equipment ID and connection against the final diagram.
Prime each liquid line with its declared solvent using its assigned pump until the outlet is bubble-free; do not introduce reactive feeds during priming.
Pressure-test with compatible inert fluid to the approved operating setpoint of 3 bar and verify stable pressure before reagents.
Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Use the declared interlocked light enclosure when one is available; otherwise verify equivalent laboratory-approved light shielding before irradiation.
Exclude ignition sources and minimize oxygen-containing organic holdup.
Route oxygen-containing off-gas and solvent vapor to the declared compatible vent when one is available.
Start liquid feeds at the canonical setpoints. Admit gas only after liquid flow, temperature, pressure, purge, and vent checks are stable.

Once the declared liquid and gas feeds, temperature and pressure are stable, close and verify the light enclosure and enable the assigned irradiation source at the final design settings. Begin the commissioning interval only after irradiation is established.

Allow an initial commissioning interval of at least 12 min, using three times the larger of the declared total reactor-time index and the sum of stage volume divided by local liquid flow. Confirm steady outlet composition and stable flow, pressure and temperature before collection; elapsed time alone does not establish steady state. Measure phase holdup or tracer response when gas or a packed bed is present. Budget additional feed for any extension before starting the run.

After measured steady state, collect a timed fraction over at least 4 min as an initial sampling interval; record exact start/end times and collected mass or volume. Extend collection if needed for the analytical method, with feed stocks scaled to the revised duration.

Collect the crude outlet in the assigned vessel and retain a labeled aliquot for conversion, selectivity, and yield analysis. This first screen ends at crude collection; no isolation work-up is authorized unless the chemist adds a confirmed downstream procedure to the intake package.
Disable irradiation before flushing or opening the light enclosure; maintain the required cooling and containment during shutdown.
Stop reactive feeds, flush each compatible line, cool the reactor to a safe handling temperature, and isolate energy sources.
Depressurize only through the controlled outlet while monitoring the pressure indicator; verify zero pressure before opening any fitting.

On leak, blockage, pressure excursion, or temperature excursion: stop reactive feeds and energy input, maintain only the hazard-appropriate purge/cooling path, isolate sources, and follow the laboratory emergency plan.
Collect product, flush, quench, and vent-associated waste in separately labeled containers compatible with the declared hazards; do not combine incompatible waste streams.

validation_experiments.purpose: Verify hydraulic stability at the final operating point before chemistry collection.
validation_experiments.procedure: Run compatible blank solvent at Q=0.25 mL/min, T=21.0 C, and BPR=3 bar for at least 10 min; record flow, temperature, pressure, leaks, and blockage indicators.

validation_experiments.purpose: Measure the residence-time distribution and phase holdup at the operating point.
validation_experiments.procedure: Introduce a compatible nonreactive tracer at Q=0.25 mL/min and measure its outlet response after correcting for external tubing delay. Report the measured mean, dispersion and liquid holdup separately from the calculated 0.342679 min index (inlet/STP apparent residence time); do not require agreement with an STP turnover index.

validation_experiments.purpose: Generate the first wet-lab response at the exact canonical design point.
validation_experiments.procedure: Execute the canonical operating procedure once and report conversion, isolated yield, selectivity, pressure trace, temperature trace, and any phase or blockage observations.

artifact_provenance.rationale_authority: Current arithmetic is independently recalculated from final settings; original scientific statements and superseded calculations are retained without treating parameter agreement as scientific validation.

intensification.basis: Predicted screening target: 20.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: mass_transfer_gas_liquid, photon_penetration. Primary flow advantage: mass_transfer. Mechanisms: gas-liquid kLa enhancement (segmented flow), photon penetration via small ID, selectivity-sensitive stream logic. Limitation-driven IF (20x) exceeds class default (6x).

diagnostic.message: No executable final design exists. Values in this diagnostic section are unapproved intermediate calculations.

residence_time_min.authority: non-executable original model rationale; arithmetic superseded by final calculation audit

source_record.text: Batch time = 5 min at 99% yield. Calculation estimated τ = 0.8 min (6× IF) but flagged O2 transfer sufficiency at only 0.19× demand and Da=92 (mass-transfer limited). Analogies 1–3 are single-phase photoredox with 12–30 min residence times — not directly applicable to this fast gas-liquid reaction. Setting τ_inlet = 4 min as conservative screening start: longer than calculation minimum (0.8 min) to compensate for O2 transfer limitation, shorter than batch (5 min) to exploit flow intensification, within 0.6–1.2 min calculation range only if O2 transfer is not limiting. Recommend screening 2–8 min. Basis: inlet/STP as required for gas-liquid design.
source_record.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

residence_time_basis.authority: non-executable original model rationale; arithmetic superseded by final calculation audit

source_record.text: Gas-liquid reagent feed present (air MFC). O2 equivalents determined by inlet/STP MFC flow only. residence_time_inlet_min = V_reactor / (Q_liq + Q_gas_STP) = 1.0 / (0.25 + 0.0833) = ~3.0 min; rounded to 4 min to account for conservative O2 transfer. In-channel time is pressure-corrected diagnostic: at 3 bar, gas compressed ~3×, so t_channel ≈ t_inlet × Q_gas_STP/(Q_gas_STP + Q_liq×3) correction gives ~2.4 min — reported as diagnostic only.
source_record.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

source_record.text: Diagnostic only. At 3 bar BPR and 21°C, in-channel gas volume compressed ~3× relative to STP. Effective in-channel gas flow ≈ 5/3 = 1.67 mL/min. t_channel = 1.0 mL / (0.25 + 1.67) mL/min ≈ 0.52 min — but this underestimates because gas is partially dissolved. Reported as ~2.4 min using intermediate estimate. Never used as primary basis.

source_record.text: Inventory: only available reactor is reactor_photo_100 at 1.0 mL. Calculation suggested 4.86 mL but that reactor does not exist in inventory. gas_flow_sccm.authority: non-executable original model rationale; arithmetic superseded by final calculation audit

source_record.text: MFC range: 0.1–10 sccm (mfc_air_10). Chemistry Plan recommends G:L = 1:1 to 2:1 at STP. At Q_liq = 0.25 mL/min = 0.25 mL/min, G:L = 1:1 requires Q_gas_STP = 0.25 mL/min = 0.25 sccm — too low for reliable MFC control. Scaling to 5 sccm gives G:L = 20:1 at STP, which is high but ensures O2 excess given transfer sufficiency warning (0.19×). Recommend screening 1–5 sccm. 5 sccm is within MFC range and safe.
